These binaries are pure Go, CGO_ENABLED=0, and byte-identical to anyone else's build of
this tag -- which is also why they carry no RandomX engine. Mainnet and the public testnet
both declare pow_engine randomx-v1, and a node that cannot verify a network's engine
`zcd version` prints the engine this binary carries; `zcd params` prints the one the
network requires. They must name the same thing.
Linux, macOS and Windows x86-64 get a second archive with -randomx in its name that
does join those networks. Scoop does not install it -- it carries the reproducible tier --
so to mine on x86-64 Windows, download zycord-<version>-windows-amd64-randomx.zip from the
release page and unzip it. Windows arm64 has no such archive: there is no cross-toolchain
for it in the runner image and no native runner, so build it yourself with
`make build-randomx` and a MinGW-w64 toolchain.
The two tiers are disjoint sets either way -- the archive you can reproduce is not the one
you can mine with. See docs/INSTALL.md, 'Two tiers of assurance'.
This package is not code-signed, and that is a decision rather than an omission: an
Authenticode certificate is a CA attesting to a verified legal identity, and this project
is published pseudonymously. What it offers instead is a build you can reproduce —
clone the repository at this tag, run `make build`, and compare the SHA-256 of bin\zcd
against SHA256SUMS.binaries in the release. See docs/INSTALL.md.
You will not see a SmartScreen warning, and the reason is worth knowing: Scoop does not
strip the mark of the web, it never attaches one. Mark-of-the-web is applied by browsers
and by the shell's attachment-execution API, not by the raw HTTP client Scoop downloads
through.
This build carries the RandomX engine and joins mainnet and the public testnet.
Windows arm64 is not offered: there is no RandomX build for it, and the pure-Go build refuses every real network.
